'''Mambillikalathil Govind Kumar Menon''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}}<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Cowsik|first=Ramanath|date=2021|title=Mambillikalathil Govind Kumar Menon. 28 August 1928—22 November 2016|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=71|pages=399–422 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2020.0013 |s2cid=237283048 |doi-access=free}}</ref> (28 August 1928&nbsp;– 22 November 2016)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/acclaimed-physicist-and-ex-isro-chief-prof-mgk-menon-dies-at-88/story-KhdZ36LxxsH1z1CasRb6CN.html|title=Acclaimed physicist and ex-ISRO chief Prof MGK Menon dies at 88|date=2016-11-22|website=[[Hindustan Times]]|language=en|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref> also known as '''M. G. K. Menon''', was an Indian [[physicist]] and policy maker who served as the [[Chairperson of ISRO]] in 1972<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.isro.gov.in/ISRO_EN/MGKMenon.html|title=MGK Menon Chairman Page |publisher= ISRO
}}</ref> and also served as the Director general of [[Defence Research and Development Organisation]] from 1974 to 1978.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.drdo.gov.in/drdo/prof-mgk-menon|title=MGK Menon page|publisher= DRDO
}}</ref> Additionally Menon has also served as the minister of state in [[Ministry of Earth Sciences]] [[Government of India]].

Born in [[Mangalore]], he attended the [[University of Bristol]] for his PhD in elementary [[particle physics]] under the guidance of [[Nobel Laureate]] [[Cecil Frank Powell|Cecil F. Powell]]. He joined the [[TIFR]] in 1955.

He undertook experiments with [[cosmic rays]] to explore the properties of [[fundamental particles]]. He was actively involved in setting up balloon flight experiments, as well as deep underground experiments with cosmic ray [[neutrinos]] in the mines at Kolar Gold Fields. He was the Director of the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]], [[Mumbai]] (1966–1975), President of the [[Indian Statistical Institute]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.isical.ac.in/officebearers.php |title=Council of the Indian Statistical Institute |access-date=14 December 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111207032145/http://www.isical.ac.in/officebearers.php |archive-date=7 December 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the Vikram Sarabhai Fellow of [[ISRO]], President of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]], Chairman Board of Governors, [[Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay]] and chairman Board of Governors of the [[Indian Institute of Information Technology, Allahabad]].

He won the [[Abdus Salam]] Award, and was a member of the [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]]. He was one of the most prominent scientists from the state of Kerala and was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in May 1970.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/fellows/|title=Lists of Royal Society Fellows|publisher=The Royal Society|access-date=18 November 2011|location=London}}</ref> The [[asteroid]] [[7564 Gokumenon]] was named in his honour in late 2008.<ref name =Nature>{{cite journal | url =https://www.nature.com/articles/nindia.2016.153 | doi= 10.1038/nindia.2016.153 | date=     23 November 2016 | title= M G K Menon: A rare Statesman of Science | first=  Somak | journal = Nature | last= Raychaudhury | access-date = 12 July 2025| doi-access=free| url-access=subscription }}</ref>{{JPL|7564|†}}

==Early life and education==
M.G.K.Menon was born into a [[Malayali]] [[Menon (subcaste)|Menon]] family to Justice Sankara Menon of Kizhakkepat and Narayanikutty Amma of Mamballikalathil.<ref name="Former minister, physicist M G K Menon passes away
">{{Cite web|url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/kerala/2016/Nov/23/former-minister-physicist-m-g-k-menon-passes-away-1541604.html |title=Former minister, physicist M G K Menon passes away |date=23 November 2016 }}</ref> He was educated at Jaswant College, [[Jodhpur]], and the [[The Institute of Science, Mumbai|Royal Institute of Science, Bombay]] (now called The Institute of Science, Mumbai), before he moved to the [[University of Bristol]] for his PhD in elementary [[particle physics]] under the guidance of [[Nobel Laureate]] [[Cecil Frank Powell|Cecil F. Powell]] in 1953.<ref name="The master conductor">{{Cite web|url=http://www.frontline.in/static/html/fl2517/stories/20080829251709300.htm|title=The master conductor|website=frontline.in|access-date=22 November 2016}}</ref>

==Career==
Menon joined [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] in 1955 "essentially because of [[Homi J. Bhabha|Bhabha]]", and the association lasted nearly five decades. He became the director of the institute in 1966, at the age of 38, following Bhabha's untimely death. In fact, Menon began handling the affairs of the institute ever since he was 33, because of Bhabha's increasing involvement with the country's nascent atomic energy programme.<ref name="The master conductor"/>

Menon was the [[Chairperson of the Indian Space Research Organisation|Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation]] in 1972 and head of the [[Defence Research and Development Organisation]] from 1974 to 1978.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.drdo.gov.in/drdo/prof-mgk-menon|title=DRDO|publisher= DRDO
}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> He was a member of the Planning Commission (1982–1989), Scientific Adviser to the Prime Minister (1986–1989) and vice-president, [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (CSIR) (1989–1990).

Menon was elected as a [[Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha]] during 1990–96. In 1989, then [[Prime Minister of India]], [[Vishwanath Pratap Singh]] appointed him as the [[Ministry of Science and Technology (India)|Minister of State for Science, Technology and Education]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Former-ISRO-chief-MGK-Menon-passes-away/articleshow/55562825.cms|title=Former ISRO chief MGK Menon passes away|date=2016-11-22|website=[[The Times of India]]|access-date=2020-02-15}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==

* He won the [[Abdus Salam Medal]] in 1996
* Special Awards: He won the [[Padma Shri]] in 1961, [[Padma Bhushan]] in 1968 and [[Padma Vibhushan]] in 1985.<ref name="Padma Awards">{{cite web|url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf|title=Padma Awards|year=2016|publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015193758/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf|archive-date=15 October 2015|access-date=3 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Padma Awards {{!}} Interactive Dashboard|url=http://www.dashboard-padmaawards.gov.in/?Year=1961-1961&Award=Padma%20Shri|access-date=2020-09-04|website=www.dashboard-padmaawards.gov.in|language=en}}</ref>
* The [[asteroid]] [[7564 Gokumenon]] was named in his honour in late 2008.<ref name =Nature/>

== Personal life ==
While working towards his PhD degree in [[particle physics]] at the [[University of Bristol]] under Professor [[C. F. Powell|Cecil F. Powell]], Menon met and married Indumati Patel, who was working towards a degree in philosophy.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Mambillikalathil Govind Kumar Menon. 28 August 1928—22 November 2016|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|date=2021 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2020.0013 |last1=Cowsik |first1=Ramanath |volume=71 |pages=399–422 |doi-access=free }}</ref> They have two children, Anant K. Menon, Professor of [[Biochemistry]] at [[Weill Cornell Medicine]] in [[New York City]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chembio.triiprograms.org/contact/|title=Tri-Institutional PhD Program in Chemical Biology|website=chembio.triiprograms.org/|access-date=24 January 2023}}</ref> and Preeti Vaid, a practicing radiologist in [[New Delhi]]. Menon has one grandchild, Kartikeya M. Menon, a resident surgeon at the Mount Sinai Hospital in New York City.
